parts.name: ground_and_roads
parts.brief:
Request, word for word: 'Now build a village in the forest. Needs unkept dirt roads like they're been driven down by horse and carriage, an empty stable, a few cottages, some scattered mediaeval props.'
YOU ARE THE GROUND PART (owner ground_and_roads, collection 'Place: ground_and_roads', stage file stage_ground_and_roads.py). You are built FIRST and alone, then frozen as ground.blend; the other five parts (forest, cottages_north, cottages_south, stable, props) are seated on you. You also MAKE the four view cameras, the sun, the fill, the world and the render settings (ownership.json: frozen.set_by). No building, no prop and no tree is yours. Read first: style-note.md (section 0, then 8), real-world-facts.json, place-settings.json (the roads, footfall and keep_clear shapes are already written: use them, change them only with a reason you state), ownership.json (every contract with you in it), acceptance.json (groups 'place: views', 'place: world', 'place: sun', 'roads'). The combine and ground-file steps are in your prompt: the ground alone goes into start.blend -> ground.blend, then the other parts are combined from that frozen file with --order both.
Make every change in ONE sweep, build the scene once and save it. For a change you are unsure of (rut depth, puddle size, hill tone steps, sun strength) write about 10 far-apart variations and draw them in ONE batch (explainer-film-place variations), at most one more batch; small quick pictures until the end.
1. THE GROUND. One continuous height field, x and y each from -900 to 900 m (z up, origin in the middle of the village), so its edge lies far behind the backdrop. Large soft relief only: inside the clearing (x -50 to 60, y -32 to 50) the land falls about 1.0 m from the north-east to the south-west so the ruts drain to a few low hollows; outside it lumps of at most 0.5 m; nothing steeper than 1 in 6 within 40 m of a building or the yard. Cut it into objects that do not overlap and have no coplanar faces within 1 mm (shared border vertices): 'Ground forest floor' (role ground.forest_floor: everything outside the clearing out to the horizon, with soft large colour variation so no 96 x 96 pixel window is flat), 'Ground clearing' (ground.grass: unkept meadow inside the clearing), 'Ground road high_road' and 'Ground road stable_lane' (ground.dirt_road), 'Ground yard' (ground.mud: the trodden stable yard, x 14 to 34, y 24 to 36), 'Ground verge ...' (ground.grass: a weedy strip about 1.2 m wide along each side of each road). Give every object its owner and role as it is made. Level pads (a footing must not float a corner): flat to within 0.25 m under each building and for 1.5 m round it: cottage A x -37.55 to -26.45, y 7.6 to 12.4 (its lean-to reaches x -40.05); B x -9.2 to -2.8, y 7.2 to 11.8; C x -29.7 to -22.3, y -12.8 to -8.2; D x 2.15 to 5.85, y -10.2 to -5.8; stable x 19.1 to 28.9, y 36 to 42. In front of the stable doorway (x 21.4 to 26.6, y 34.6 to 36.8) the yard is level to within 0.15 m.
2. THE ROADS (unkept, driven by a horse and cart). Run the kit's roads step from the 'roads' entries of place-settings.json inside your stage, so the frozen ground already holds the ruts (the kit remembers each vertex's own height, so finish can run it again without digging twice). High road: 5.0 m wide, ruts 1.4 m apart and 0.12 m deep with a bank beside each (about a third of the depth), hoof prints down the middle (about 0.13 m across, one about every 0.9 m, left and right in turn), a grass crown in the middle, puddle hollows in some rut bottoms. Lane: 3.4 m wide, ruts 0.09 m deep, same gauge, ends in the yard at about (24.3, 34.2). Add 2 or 3 potholes on the high road between x -70 and 20 (0.3 to 0.6 m across, 6 to 10 cm deep, puddle hollows) and 2 in the yard, with hoof prints and ruts across the yard to the doorway. The road wobbles a few centimetres and bends away at both ends so the trees can hide where it goes. The road must read as unkept and driven on at 600 pixels wide from View road_eye: measure the ruts by rays (the audit's roads check). Nothing grows on a wheel track or in a puddle hollow (the kit's gates do it; check the counts are exactly 0).
3. THE FOUR CAMERAS (names exact; render 1200 x 800; clip start 0.1 m; clip end 2000 m or more and never under the figure the audit names for each camera). Start values, adjust by up to 3 m sideways or 1 m up and report the final numbers: 'View wide' at (-48, -30, 14.0) looking at (-5, 14, 2.0), 28 mm: all four cottages, the well (-17.5, 6), the lane junction (20, 2), the stable (24, 39) and about 100 m of road must be inside the frame (project their centres through the camera to check; if the stable is out, move the camera back or up, never move a building). This is the first view: it shows the most of what the person asked for. 'View road_eye' at (-62, -3.7, 1.7) on the road crown at the west entrance looking at (-20, 0.5, 1.5), 35 mm: ruts, hoof prints, a puddle and the grass crown in the foreground, cottages A and C ahead. 'View stable_close' at (28.5, 25.5, 1.7) looking at (24, 36, 1.4), 28 mm: the open doorway, yard mud with hoof prints, the trough and the hitching rail. 'View cottage_close' at (-14, 0.3, 1.7) looking at (-31, 8, 1.6), 35 mm: cottage A's front, the well and its barrels. The forest builder keeps these sightlines clear.
4. THE WORLD ROUND THE PLACE (the audit's check 'place: world'). Every view must see a finished horizon, not empty sky above a dark slab or the edge of the ground. Make an all-round backdrop of real shapes: three closed rings of hills with a lumpy tree-line skyline (role backdrop), near ring about 380 to 520 m from the middle, 25 to 45 m high, colour about #4F6A4A; middle ring 520 to 680 m, 45 to 75 m, about #6C8776; far ring 680 to 820 m, 70 to 110 m, about #8FA6B5: lighter and bluer when far, no gap in any direction (overlap the rings), each ring with 3 to 5 tone steps (tree-line bands, ridge shading) so no 96 x 96 pixel window below the sky is flat. Plain colour that does not take light and casts no shadow (turn shadow off on every backdrop object): use a flat, rough, no-emission colour if you can, because an emission shader makes the renderer rule pick Cycles; if the look needs emission say so in your report. Continue the plain forest-floor ground to about 900 m each way (its edge at least 80 m beyond the far ring's outer foot, hidden), a gradient sky (about #9DB7CC at the top to #D9E2E6 at the horizon) and NO haze or fog volume. Backdrop objects: at most 3 meshes under 60,000 triangles.
5. LIGHT. One sun lamp only, warm (about #FFF1D6), from the south-east (compass 135 degrees, the direction it shines from) about 50 degrees up, soft shadow edge (1 to 2 degrees), strength by eye so the clearing is bright but under 0.5 percent of dots are clipped; plus a soft cool fill (a wide area lamp on the camera side, or more sky), never a second sun lamp. No other lamps, no lit window, no glow: nothing lit, so EEVEE.
6. BUDGET AND REPORT. At most 20 mesh objects, 700,000 triangles (the kit makes the ruts fine itself, at most 150,000 faces). In ground_promise say what the ground promises the others: level pads under every building, a level yard in front of the stable doorway, ruts 9 to 12 cm deep, nobody builds within 3.1 m of the high road's centre line or 2.3 m of the lane's, the cameras and the sun never change. Say which of the audit's roads and world checks you saw pass.
steps_in_order: Make the empty start scene and the ground: the graded height field, the level pads, the role objects without overlaps, the forest floor out to the horizon
Shape the two roads, the stable yard, the verges, the potholes and puddle hollows with the kit's roads step (ruts 1.4 m apart, banks, hoof prints, grass crown); check the ruts by rays
Make the four cameras (View wide, View road_eye, View stable_close, View cottage_close), the sun, the soft fill and the sky colours; check every item named for View wide is inside its frame
Make the three backdrop rings, hide the ground's edge, set every clip end, check 'place: world' and 'place: sun' pass (no emission, no haze, no flat windows)
Character: weedy verges, mud colour in the ruts, drier banks, then run finish-part, the construction check, the stage twice, and the ownership check; save ground.blend

parts.name: forest
parts.brief:
Request, word for word: 'Now build a village in the forest. Needs unkept dirt roads like they're been driven down by horse and carriage, an empty stable, a few cottages, some scattered mediaeval props.'
YOU ARE THE FOREST PART (owner forest, collection 'Place: forest', stage file stage_forest.py; object names start Tree, Bush, Fern, Log, Stump, Rock). You build the forest round the village on the frozen ground. Read first: style-note.md (sections 0, 1, 4, 8), real-world-facts.json (tree_height, tree_crown_and_trunk), place-settings.json, ownership.json (your contracts with the ground, the cottages, the stable and the props), acceptance.json (groups 'forest' and 'place: sun'). Make every change in ONE sweep, build the scene once and save it; for a change you are unsure of (crown lumpiness, tree density, tone mix) write about 10 far-apart variations and draw them in ONE batch (explainer-film-place variations), at most one more batch.
WHAT TO BUILD
- Trees all round, from the clearing's rim (about 30 m from the middle) out to about 150 m: at least 70 trees, about 60 percent broadleaf (oak, beech: trunk 0.35 to 0.9 m across, 14 to 24 m tall, a crown of 3 to 5 chunky lumps) and 40 percent pine (straight trunk 0.3 to 0.7 m across, 16 to 30 m tall, 4 to 6 stacked cones in the top half). Big simple masses, never leaf clouds. Each tree is a trunk (role tree.bark, tapered, with a root flare that rests ON the ground within 2 cm, never buried) and a crown (role plant.foliage) that overlaps the trunk top by at least 0.2 m so it is carried. About 12 hero trees (the nearest to the four cameras and to the clearing's rim) are one trunk object and one crown object each; the rest are clusters, one trunk object and one crown object holding 3 to 6 separate trees (loose pieces). Budget: at most 160 objects, 500,000 triangles in all, no mesh over 300,000.
- Undergrowth: 25 to 40 bushes and ferns at the rim and beside the road outside the clearing (plant.foliage, joined into at most 20 objects); 6 stumps and 4 fallen logs (role tree.bark, 0.3 to 0.6 m high, mossy, at the rim, never on a road, no closer than 6 m to the stable); 8 mossy boulders (stone.rock, 0.4 to 1.2 m).
- The road must disappear into the trees: the high road bends away at both ends (see the roads in place-settings.json) and goes out of sight behind tree groups at about 100 to 130 m; from |x| about 55 outward there are tight groups of trunks and undergrowth on both sides, 3 to 6 m from the road's edge (shade there is intended), never on the road's dirt strip or within 2.0 m of its centre line.
- Inside the clearing (x -50 to 60, y -32 to 50): trees only at its rim, at least 10 m from any road edge, at least 14 m from any wall, never inside the stable yard and never on the south-east side of a building (the sun comes from the south-east about 50 degrees up; shadows point north-west and are 0.84 times the height long; the audit's 'place: sun' check names the object that shades most). No crown touches a roof.
- Keep every view camera's sightline clear (read the camera objects in the frozen ground file): View wide at about (-48, -30, 14) looks at (-5, 14, 2); View road_eye at (-62, -3.7, 1.7) looks east; View stable_close at (28.5, 25.5, 1.7) looks north; View cottage_close at (-14, 0.3, 1.7) looks north-west. No trunk or crown within 6 m of a line of sight unless it is a planned foreground tree that frames the picture.
- Look: trees lived_in (the ground round them is neglected): moss low on the north side of trunks, a few big designed marks (a scar, a hollow) and not bark noise; foliage in 3 to 4 dark greens (#3F5A32 family), one or two golden-brown trees allowed; faceted chunky forms, bevels where a hand could touch.
ROLES: tree.bark (trunks, stumps, logs), plant.foliage (crowns, bushes, ferns), stone.rock (boulders). YOU MAKE: no prop, no building part, no ground. DO NOT TOUCH: the ground, cameras, lights, world, the cottages, the stable and the props.
steps_in_order: The about 12 hero trees nearest the cameras and the clearing rim, seated on the ground, with the road-end tree groups that hide where the road goes
The tree clusters all round out to about 150 m, kept clear of the roads, walls, yard and camera sightlines
Undergrowth at the rim (bushes, ferns), 6 stumps, 4 fallen logs, 8 mossy boulders
Character (moss, a few big designed marks, no two trees alike), roles, finish-part pass, construction check, stage twice, ownership check
If time: a second tone mix of crowns and a few leaning or broken trees at the clearing's rim

parts.brief:

Object names start 'Cottage A ...' and 'Cottage B ...'. Another builder, cottages_south, makes cottages C and D from the same facts at the same time: copy nothing from them. Read first: style-note.md (sections 0, 1, 2, 3, 8), real-world-facts.json (door_height, bay_free_span, thatch_pitch, thatch_thickness, wall_thickness, cottage_bay, cottage_eaves_height, wattle_stud_spacing, sleeper_wall_width), place-settings.json, ownership.json, acceptance.json (group 'cottages'). Make every change in ONE sweep, build the scene once and save it; for a change you are unsure of (thatch roll, chip amount, sag) write about 10 far-apart variations and draw them in ONE batch (explainer-film-place variations), at most one more batch.
COMMON TO BOTH (a mediaeval north-west European cottage: timber frame or stone, wattle and daub, thatch): build from the ground up, every part carried: a stone footing (role stone.footing, 0.3 to 0.5 m wide, 0.25 to 0.4 m high) under the walls, a sill timber on it, posts, a wall plate (the object name contains 'wall plate'), studs 0.45 to 0.9 m apart, wall panels, rafters resting on a purlin (name contains 'purlin') and a ridge piece (name contains 'ridge'), a floor.earth floor inside the walls (top 0.05 m above the ground, so the doorway looks onto something), a door leaf (timber.door) on iron hinges (iron.fitting) with a flat stone doorstep (stone.step, rise 0.12 to 0.2 m), 2 or 3 small shuttered windows (opening about 0.45 x 0.6 m, shutter leaves timber.shutter about 0.6 m high, one standing ajar, NO glass). Beams: planks and boards span at most 1.38 m, beams and fences at most 2.5 m, except a wall plate, ridge, purlin, tie or collar between two trusses or walls, which may span up to 3.9 m (the bay_free_span fact): place a truss at least every 3.7 m. Rafters need a purlin so they have no free stretch over 2.5 m. Character as SHAPE: no two posts alike, posts a little out of plumb, ridge sagging 2 to 4 cm between trusses, thatch lumpy with a rolled eave, a few boards replaced in a fresher colour. Everything stands on the frozen ground (pk.seat_on_ground); the ground part gave you a level pad under each building. Props are NOT yours (no barrel, bucket, bench, woodpile, ladder, sack, jug): the props part makes them. Object budget: at most 75 objects per cottage, about 100,000 triangles for each.
COTTAGE A (the long one, centre (-32, 10)): footprint 11.1 x 4.8 m (x -37.55 to -26.45, y 7.6 to 12.4), 3 bays of 3.7 m so 4 truss lines; eaves 2.0 m; walls wall.timber_frame: dark oak frame (#3E3128) with CREAM limewash panels (#CDBE9A), 4 or 5 panels with big chips showing the wattle (a few hazel rods as shapes) and a darker splash band at the foot; roof roof.thatch, golden (#9C7A3F) at 50 degrees, 0.3 m thick, eave overhang 0.45 m, ridge about 4.9 m, a darker ridge cap; door in the south wall at x -32 (1.7 m high, 0.85 m wide); two shuttered windows in the south wall (x -35 and -29) and one in the north wall; a LOG STORE LEAN-TO on the west end, 2.5 m deep (x -40.05 to -37.55) and 3.4 m wide (y 8.1 to 11.5), posts and a roof.shingle monopitch at 32 degrees, open to the south and EMPTY (the props part stacks the woodpile outside it).
COTTAGE B (small and heavy, centre (-6, 9.5)): footprint 6.4 x 4.6 m (x -9.2 to -2.8, y 7.2 to 11.8), 2 bays of 3.2 m (one central truss); walls wall.stone, grey rubble in big uneven blocks, 0.5 m thick, about 2.1 m to the eaves with stone gables up to the ridge, quoin stones at the corners; a timber lintel (name 'lintel', timber.beam) over the door; door in the south wall at x -6.0 (1.65 m high, 0.85 m wide); one small shuttered window in the south wall and one in the east wall (0.4 x 0.5 m); roof roof.thatch, OLD grey-green and mossy at 50 degrees, 0.35 m thick, eave overhang 0.4 m; the only STONE CHIMNEY (role stone.chimney, base about 0.9 x 0.7 m) on the EAST gable, built up from its footing through the gable and standing 1.2 m above the ridge: no smoke, no glow, no lamp.
TELL THEM APART: A is long, cream, golden thatch with a lean-to; B is small, grey stone, dark mossy thatch and a chimney. Neither looks like cottage C (red-ochre panels) or D (pale cob, silver shingles).
ROLES: wall.timber_frame, wall.stone, roof.thatch, roof.shingle (lean-to), timber.post, timber.beam, timber.door, timber.shutter, timber.plank (lean-to boards), stone.footing, stone.step, stone.chimney, floor.earth, iron.fitting. DO NOT TOUCH: the ground, cameras, lights, world, and every other part's objects.
steps_in_order: Cottage A and cottage B walls from the ground up: footing, sill, posts, wall plate, panels or stone, floor.earth, door, doorstep (carried, real sizes, level pad)
Roofs of A and B: rafters, purlin, ridge, thatch with a rolled eave, the stone chimney on B
Shutters and windows, hinges, the log-store lean-to on A, the lintel on B
Character as shape (no two parts alike, sag, chipped plaster showing wattle, replaced boards), roles, finish-part pass, construction check, stage twice, ownership check
If time: wattle rods in the chips, a drip line and mud splash as shapes, small timber details (pegs, latch)

parts.name: stable
parts.brief:
Request, word for word: 'Now build a village in the forest. Needs unkept dirt roads like they're been driven down by horse and carriage, an empty stable, a few cottages, some scattered mediaeval props.'
YOU ARE THE STABLE PART (owner stable, collection 'Place: stable', stage file stage_stable.py; object names start 'Stable ...'). You build the EMPTY STABLE, the most detailed building (View stable_close looks at it), its yard fittings and nothing else. Read first: style-note.md (sections 0, 1, 2, 6, 7 point 7, 8), real-world-facts.json (door_height, door_width, fence_height, shingle_pitch, bay_free_span, box_stall_size, stable_eaves_and_ceiling, manger_and_rack_height, horse_height_withers), place-settings.json, ownership.json (contracts with ground, forest, props), acceptance.json (group 'stable'). Make every change in ONE sweep, build the scene once and save it; for a change you are unsure of (door leaf sag, board colours, shingle gaps) write about 10 far-apart variations and draw them in ONE batch (explainer-film-place variations), at most one more batch.
THE BUILDING (centre (24, 39), the long side faces south onto the yard): outer footprint 9.8 x 6.0 m (x 19.1 to 28.9, y 36.0 to 42.0). Stone dwarf wall (stone.footing, 0.3 to 0.5 m wide, 0.3 to 0.45 m high) under all walls, with a gap at the doorway where a sill stone (stone.step, 0.10 m above the floor) lies. Walls: a timber frame (timber.post about 0.2 m square, a wall plate named 'wall plate' at 2.4 m, truss lines at x 19.1, 22.4, 25.6 and 28.9) clad in near-black UPRIGHT BOARDS (timber.plank, boards 0.15 to 0.3 m wide, different widths, silvered edges, 4 or 5 boards replaced in a fresher colour, a gap or two). Cladding may be one object per wall holding separate boards (loose pieces), so the scale check skips it. Stalls: THREE empty box stalls against the back (north) wall, each about 3.1 to 3.2 m wide and 3.05 m deep (x 19.3 to 22.4, 22.4 to 25.6, 25.6 to 28.7; y 38.75 to 41.8), partitions on the truss lines 2.2 m high (boards to 1.4 m, open rails above; role timber.fence; no free rail longer than 2.5 m), stall fronts open (no rail unless a post stands every 2.5 m). Aisle 2.4 to 2.55 m wide along the front (y 36.2 to 38.7). Ties across the building (names contain 'tie', timber.beam) rest on the wall plates and on posts at the stall-front line (y 38.7), so each stretch is at most 3.9 m. Each stall: an EMPTY manger on the back wall (timber.generic box about 1.0 x 0.4 m with its rim at 1.0 to 1.2 m, standing on two short posts on the floor), an EMPTY hay rack above it (timber.fence rails, bottom at about 1.5 m, fixed to the wall) and an iron tie ring at 1.5 m (iron.fitting). Floor: floor.earth, beaten earth, flush with the ground (top at ground level), with a shallow gutter if you like. Doorway: centred at x 24.0 in the south wall, 2.4 m wide and 2.3 m high, a lintel (name 'lintel', at most 2.5 m long), TWO door leaves (timber.door, 1.2 m wide, 2.3 m high, on iron hinges) standing OPEN: one fully open against the outside wall, one hanging half open and sagging a little on its hinges. Two small slatted vents high in the gable ends. Request, word for word: 'Now build a village in the forest. Needs unkept dirt roads like they're been driven down by horse and carriage, an empty stable, a few cottages, some scattered mediaeval props.'
YOU ARE THE PROPS PART (owner props, collection 'Place: props', stage file stage_props.py; object names start 'Prop ...'). You make the SCATTERED MEDIAEVAL PROPS of the village: all of them, so that the cottages and the stable stay clean of them. RULES: scatter them, never in a line: groups of two or three beside doors and walls, singles at the road edge, one story per hand-span. Each prop rests on the frozen ground (pk.seat_on_ground) or on another prop, and is carried (a leaning ladder or spare wheel is carried by the ground at its foot). plan.renderer_hint: EEVEE is expected: the plan has no lamp, no lit window, no fire, no glowing material and no water object (daylight sun and sky only; the trough is a dry hollowed log, puddles are hollows in the ground), so the rule in renderer-for finds nothing lit. One caution: the role backdrop wants a plain unlit colour, and if the ground builder makes it with an emission shader the rule reads that as a glowing material and picks Cycles. The brief asks for a flat, rough, no-emission colour so EEVEE is kept; if emission is needed the builder says so, Cycles is accepted and the card time is counted against the 150-minute total. Renderer wished: auto.
open_questions: Period and country: the request names none. I assumed a north-west European mediaeval village (timber frame with wattle and daub, rubble stone, cob, thatch and wooden shingles, 13th to 15th century). If the person pictures log cabins (Scandinavian or Slavic) the cottage walls and roofs change.

'Horse and carriage': read as horse-drawn carts and wagons (a gauge of 1.4 m, a one-horse cart). No measured mediaeval gauge was found (sources: Roman-era and Bronze Age figures, popular summaries), so the gauge is weak. If a wider coach is meant, raise the gauge in place-settings.json (the facts range 1.2 to 1.5 m would also need changing).

Backdrop colour and the renderer: the backdrop must be 'plain unlit colour'; an emission shader makes the kit's renderer rule pick Cycles (more card time). The brief asks for a flat no-emission colour to keep EEVEE; ask the person if they would rather accept Cycles for a flatter, truly unlit backdrop.

Numbers I could NOT confirm with a real source (all weak or guess in real-world-facts.json): the mediaeval cart gauge; hoof-print size for a DRAUGHT horse (only pony to Thoroughbred widths 85 to 132 mm were found; the kit's dimple is fixed at about 0.13 m and cannot be set per road); the size of mediaeval stalls (modern 10 x 10 to 12 x 12 ft figures, I used 3.05 m); peasant door heights (one V&A note about better houses); wood shingle pitch (from memory); cask heights (computed from volumes); undated cart wheel sizes; manger and rack heights; road widths; wattle hurdle, well and small prop sizes; tree crown ratios.

'A few cottages' is taken as four, 'some scattered props' as 14 kinds and about 70 to 90 objects, 'empty stable' as no animals, no hay and no people in it (a few loose straws only). Tell me if any count is wrong.
The 3.9 m bay_free_span fact lets wall plates, ridge pieces, purlins and ties span a 3.7 m bay (judged from one survey, weak). Confirm it, or the builders must add posts nobody would build.
The trough is a dry hollowed log (timber.generic) and the well has no water object, because a water object makes the renderer rule choose Cycles; say if a water-filled trough is wanted.

The 'place: sun' check: with the sun from the south-east at 50 degrees, the forest that stands beside the road outside the clearing (|x| above about 55) shades it by design; the audit may report more than half of some view's ground in shade as a LOOK. I kept trees 10 m or more from the roads inside the clearing to avoid it.
Object count: about 600 to 700 planned objects against the audit's LOOK line of 1000; if the forest or props builders go over, the audit says LOOK, above 3000 FAIL.

No concept pictures from the painter were planned or priced: this run allows no paid image step. If the person wants them, the garden's cost was 29 calls, US$3.86 (measured in that job); the person must say yes first.
plan.notes: I read the planner file, the skill (SKILL.md, the-required-steps, construction-and-scale, style-rule-and-measures, the worked examples, batched-rounds-and-card-time), the four templates, the village preset, the canal-lock example files and the kit's own code for settings, roads, masks, the scale check, the ownership check and the renderer rule, so that the plan fits what the tools read. I wrote the five plan files (style-note.md, real-world-facts.json, place-settings.json, ownership.json, acceptance.json) into the plan folder and wrote the person's 150-minute card total into the ledger (card-time start; it shows 150 min, 0 s used). The planner used no card time and touched no Blender scene. place-settings.json passes the kit's own validator with no problem and no road warning (measured); the other three JSON files parse (measured). Nothing else was run or measured: sizes are judged from the sources named in each fact row, none is strong.\nTHE PLAN: place 'forest village', type village, look lived_in with every ground role neglected (the person's 'unkept', through look_by_role), state damp (shaded forest ground). Six parts: ground_and_roads (built first, frozen; also makes the 4 cameras, the sun and soft fill, the world, the three backdrop rings of hills, the graded ground to about 900 m, the two roads with ruts 1.4 m apart, banks, hoof prints, grass crown, potholes and the stable yard), forest (70+ trees, undergrowth, stumps, logs, boulders; hides where the road goes), cottages_north (A long cream timber frame with golden thatch and a log-store lean-to; B small grey rubble stone with mossy thatch and the only stone chimney), cottages_south (C red-ochre daub, pale thatch, tall door; D small pale cob with silver shingles), stable (9.8 x 6.0 m near-black boards, dark mossy shingles, 2.4 m open double doorway, three empty box stalls with empty mangers and hay racks, a dry hollowed-log trough, a bare hitching rail) and props (well with windlass, 5 barrels, crates, sacks, buckets, a parked two-wheeled cart with shafts down, woodpile and chopping block, haystack, wattle hurdles, bench, jugs, baskets, handbarrow, ladder). Count of the request's nouns: village (the whole), forest (forest part plus backdrop), dirt roads (ground, with ruts and hoof prints for the horse and cart), empty stable (stable), a few cottages (four), scattered mediaeval props (props): each lands in a part.\nViews: 4, each 1200 x 800 (not for the film): wide (named first: it shows roads, cottages, stable, props and forest), road_eye, stable_close, cottage_close. The ground part's brief holds the world round the place (backdrop rings, ground to the horizon, edge hidden, clip end 2000 m or more, no haze volume) and the camera spots with the items each must frame; the backdrop must also avoid flat windows (the style rule's flat-window line), which I wrote into its brief. The facts research found most numbers only weakly (see open_questions). Things I added that you might not expect: a free_span fact of 3.9 m so cruck-style bays do not need invented posts; a trough that is a dry hollowed log, and a well with no water, to keep the renderer on EEVEE; no sign or lettering anywhere (the audit's lettering check); the straw scraps in the stable are made by props, not the stable, to keep material ownership clean (roles shared between parts, such as timber.post, are left without material patterns in ownership.json, as in the canal-lock example; if ownership-diff complains about shared PK materials, the integrator should say so). Not tested: that the cameras really frame what the brief lists, that the plan's budgets hold, that the 3.9 m free span fact passes the audit's judge, and that look_by_role with 'ground.*' behaves as the README describes (the validator accepts it).
